To enhance the robustness and accuracy of entity recognition, we utilized an ensemble of four fine-tuned pre-trained language models, each trained with diverse hyperparameter configurations. The outputs of these individual NER models were aggregated using a voting mechanism to yield a consensus set of extracted entities. Following entity extraction, we implemented a comprehensive entity cleaning and normalization procedure. This involved employing the Abbreviation Plus Pseudo-Precision method to resolve abbreviations and integrating data from established resources such as MeSH and PubTator for robust synonym mapping and entity standardization. Subsequently, we performed Relation Extraction (RE) to identify and categorize the semantic relationships between the extracted entities. We developed both single-sentence and multi-sentence RE models, fine-tuning PubMedBERT with multiple hyperparameter settings and combining the results through a voting strategy to maximize the reliability of the extracted relationships. Finally, to enrich the relational structure of our knowledge representation, we integrated entity linkage information from external, curated databases such as Hetionet, thereby constructing a comprehensive domain knowledge graph. While our primary analysis focuses on the paper level, we acknowledge that future research could fruitfully explore the knowledge entity level to provide even finer-grained insights. Utilizing the constructed domain knowledge graph, we proceeded to build a paper-level network, denoted as G_K = (V_K, E_K), where each paper v ∈ V_K represents a node. An edge (u, v) ∈ E_K signifies a connection between two papers, established either through the sharing of one or more identical knowledge entities or through the existence of any relational link between their constituent entities within the domain knowledge graph. Furthermore, to capture the semantic content of each paper, we computed a 300-dimensional word embedding vector for each identified knowledge entity using PubMedBERT. A central embedding vector x_v for each paper v was then derived to represent its overall knowledge content.
